settings.text:
Join Grandmaster Timothy W. Hogan and Patricia Awyan Lehman on a sacred journey through Ancient Egypt—where the wisdom of the Pharaohs, the mysteries of the Templars, and the echoes of Atlantis converge. Walk beneath the gaze of the Sphinx, stand within the Great Pyramid, and enter sanctuaries long sealed by time. This is a pilgrimage for seekers called to awaken the ancient light within, to remember the lineage of the Ark of the Covenant, and to walk the timeless path of initiation.

You will explore legendary temples, descend into royal tombs, wander the colossal halls of Karnak, sail to sacred islands, and witness the treasures of the new Grand Egyptian Museum—all guided by two wisdom keepers who illuminate the deeper meanings encoded in these ancient sites.

If Egypt has been calling to your spirit, this is your invitation to answer through a once-in-a-lifetime journey into the heart of its timeless legacy.

“May the eternal flame guide your steps.”

settings.title: Saqqara, the Serapeum, & the Sound Healing Hospital
settings.dropdown_text: Descend into the shadowed passages of Saqqara, home to the Step Pyramid of Djoser and the mystical Unas Pyramid. Explore the vast underground Serapeum, where colossal granite sarcophagi rest in silence, echoing with ancient power. Then, step into the remarkable Sound Healing Hospital, an ancient chamber built with extraordinary acoustics, where resonance and vibration once played a role in healing and initiation.

settings.title: Temple of Hathor at Dendera
settings.dropdown_text: Gaze upon the celestial Dendera Zodiac, discover stargates and the mystery of the melted stairs. Dedicated to Hathor, the goddess of love, joy, music, dance, fertility, beauty, and the stars. She is often depicted as a woman with the horns of a cow cradling the solar disk, symbolizing her role as the celestial mother who carries the sun across the heavens.

settings.title: Karnak & Luxor Temples
settings.dropdown_text: Connected in antiquity by the Avenue of the Sphinxes, Karnak and Luxor formed the spiritual heart of ancient Thebes. At Karnak, you will wander through the awe-inspiring Hypostyle Hall, stand before colossal statues, and visit the Sacred Lake once used in priestly rituals. At Luxor, especially enchanting at twilight, you’ll explore its grand colonnades and inner sanctuaries, a temple dedicated not to gods of the afterlife but to the renewal of kingship and divine power. Together, these temples reveal the eternal union of heaven and earth.

settings.title: Edfu & Kom Ombo Temples
settings.dropdown_text: Journey along the Nile to two of Egypt’s most captivating sanctuaries. At Edfu, step inside the best-preserved temple in all of Egypt, dedicated to Horus the falcon god, where towering pylons and richly carved walls bring myth and ritual vividly to life. At Kom Ombo, explore the unique double temple, honoring both Horus and Sobek, the crocodile god. With its twin sanctuaries, medical carvings, and sacred crocodile mummies, Kom Ombo offers a rare glimpse into the duality of Egyptian belief.

settings.title: Valley of the Kings
settings.dropdown_text: Enter the legendary Valley of the Kings, where over sixty tombs were carved into the limestone cliffs to house the pharaohs of the New Kingdom. Here you may encounter the celebrated tomb of Tutankhamun, whose excavated golden treasures astonished the modern world; the vast and intricate tomb of Seti I; the richly decorated chambers of Ramses II, Ramses III, and Ramses VI; and many others whose walls are alive with colorful hieroglyphs.

settings.title: Iconic Sightseeing Experiences
settings.subheading: Together, these iconic sites create a journey that bridges the history, myth, and mystery of the Lost Arks, inviting you into the heart of ancient Egypt in a way few travelers ever experience.

settings.title: Day 1 – Saturday, March 28: Arrival in Cairo
settings.text: Warm welcome at Cairo International Airport, visa assistance, transfer to Hyatt Regency West Hotel, introductory meeting & welcome dinner.

settings.title: Day 2 – Sunday, March 29: Giza Plateau & the Sphinx
settings.text: Explore the Giza Plateau, Valley Temple, panoramic view lunch at 9 Pyramids Lounge, and exclusive access between the paws of the Sphinx.

settings.title: Day 3 – Monday, March 30: Saqqara & the Serapeum
settings.text: Visit the Step Pyramid, Unas Pyramid, vast underground Serapeum, and the unique Sound Healing Hospital.

settings.title: Day 4 – Tuesday, March 31: Cairo & Flight to Luxor
settings.text: Tour the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization, explore Coptic Cairo and the Hanging Church, then fly to Luxor.

settings.title: Day 5 – Wednesday, April 1: Dendera & Luxor Temple
settings.text: Discover the Temple of Hathor at Dendera with its famous Zodiac, and walk the grand halls of Luxor Temple, enchanting at twilight.

settings.title: Day 6 – Thursday, April 2: Abydos & the Osirian
settings.text: Full-day excursion with special private permission to the Temple of Seti I and the mysterious Osirian.

settings.title: Day 7 – Friday, April 3: Valley of the Kings & Nobles
settings.text: Explore pharaonic tombs including Tutankhamun and Seti I, see vibrant Tombs of the Nobles, the Temple of Hatshepsut, and the Alabaster Museum.

settings.title: Day 8 – Saturday, April 4: Karnak Temple
settings.text: Wander Karnak’s colossal Hypostyle Hall and Sacred Lake. Private Access Temple of Sekhmet, Optional sunrise hot air balloon ride over Luxor.

settings.title: Day 9 – Sunday, April 5: Edfu & Kom Ombo
settings.text: Drive south to Aswan, visiting Edfu Temple, dedicated to Horus, and Kom Ombo, a double temple honoring Horus and Sobek.

settings.title: Day 10 – Monday, April 6: Elephantine Island & Optional Excursions
settings.text: Sail to sacred Elephantine Island. Optional afternoon visits to Abu Simbel or the Nubian Museum.

settings.title: Day 11 – Tuesday, April 7: Aswan Quarry & Temple of Isis at Philae
settings.text: See the colossal Unfinished Obelisk at Aswan Quarry, then take a boat to the enchanting Temple of Isis at Philae. Evening flight to Cairo.

settings.title: Day 12 – Wednesday, April 8: Grand Egyptian Museum
settings.text: Visit the spectacular new museum, home to Tutankhamun’s treasures and Egypt’s greatest collection. Afternoon free. Evening Lecture.

settings.title: Day 13 – Thursday, April 9: Great Pyramid Private Entry
settings.text: Culmination of the journey: exclusive two-hour private entry inside the Great Pyramid, with access to all three chambers. {2 hours Templar Only}

settings.title: Day 14 – Friday, April 10: Departure
settings.text: Transfer to Cairo International Airport for international flights home.

settings.title: Day 7 – Monday, February 9th - Nile Cruise & Valley of Kings & Queens
settings.text:
• Overnight in Luxor on Royal Lily Cruise
  • Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner included

Visit the west bank and see the most breathtaking beautifully preserved tomb in Egypt of Queen Nefertari in the Valley of the Queens.
settings.dropdown_text:
After this, we continue to experience the exquisite Temple of the female pharaoh Hatshepsut, one of the most beautiful masterpieces of the ancient world. Return to Cruise for Lunch.

We then continue to the Valley of the Kings with its deep subterranean tombs of the ancient Kings of Egypt.

settings.title: Day 8 – Tuesday, February 10th - Nile Cruise & Temples
settings.text:
• Overnight in Qena on Royal Lily Cruise
  • Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner included

Early morning visit to Karnak and a PRIVATE VISIT to see the Shrine of Sekhmet. We will explore Karnak Temple with its huge columns that reach to the stars.
settings.dropdown_text:
It was said that the ancient ones built these columns with special stones to collect and store the energies of their sacred singing and chanting that was done daily at dawn as the priests and priestess walked down the processional path to the Holies of Holies. Then daily the stored energy within the columns would fill the Temple spaces, energizing those who visited this sacred Temple throughout the day. We will be at the Seven Gates to Heaven door at Osiris temple.

Sail to Qena. After lunch we will visit Denderah Temple dedicated to Hathor, Goddess of love and joy. Experience the famous circular zodiac ceiling and secret crypts with enigmatic images. Denderah Temple was considered a university of higher learning and ancient Stargate and is still alive today.

settings.title: Day 9 – Wednesday, February 11th - Nile Cruise & Abydos
settings.text:
• Overnight in Luxor on Royal Lily Cruise
  • Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner included

After breakfast, we drive by bus to visit Abydos. This amazing, beautiful Temple built by Seti I was dedicated to Osiris. It was considered a profound pilgrimage place and over the centuries pilgrims came with offering pots to ask for a blessing from the beloved god Osiris.
settings.dropdown_text:
Today it is one of the most amazing sites in Egypt. Abydos Temple was considered a university of higher learning and ancient Stargate and is still alive today.

We will have a PRIVATE VISIT to see the ancient mysterious Osireion mythological structure. Return for lunch and then sail back to Luxor.

settings.title: Day 10 – Thursday, February 12th - Sailing The Nile
settings.text:
• Overnight in Aswan on Royal Lily Cruise
  • Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner included
settings.dropdown_text: Full day sailing on the Nile as we make our way back to Aswan, relaxing, integrating and deepening our experience of the tour. We will end the day with Galabia Party and festive Farewell Dinner for the Lower Nile cruise.

settings.subtitle: Tour Host
settings.title: Timothy W. Hogan, Grandmaster of the Knights Templar
settings.text:
Timothy W. Hogan stands as a luminous presence within the Western Mystery Tradition—a Grand Master of the Order of the Temple of Secret Initiates, and a bridge between ancient initiatory lineages and today’s spiritual seekers Gaiacontactinthedesert.com.

With decades of study and initiation in Freemasonry, Rosicrucianism, Martinism, and Templar orders, Tim has dedicated his life to reviving the sacred teachings of these traditions for the modern soul GaiaScribd. He is author of deeply influential works such as The Alchemical Keys to Masonic Ritual, The Way of the Templar, The 32 Secret Paths of Solomon, and Entering the Chain of Union—each exploring the spiritual architecture behind ritual, symbol, and initiation Gaiacontactinthedesert.com.

A sought-after lecturer and emissary of wisdom, Timothy has spoken at universities, embassies, and Masonic bodies across the globe, and has graced screens and airwaves through television, podcasts, and documentary series—including Gaia’s own Mysteries of the Knights Templar and Ancient Civilizations Gaiacontactinthedesert.comEverand.

Bringing rare and sacred insights into the Yucatán Adventure journey, Tim serves as both guide and initiate—ready to lead you beyond the surface into a realm of remembrance, renewal, and awakening.

settings.subtitle: Speaker
settings.title: Patricia Awyan Lehman
settings.text:
Director, Speaker, Researcher, Explorer, and Symbologist — Horus Rising

Patricia Awyan Lehman is the Director of Horus Rising — a speaker, researcher, explorer, and symbologist. A lifelong student of metaphysical, spiritual, and indigenous traditions, Patricia’s diverse background blends ancient wisdom with modern understanding. Her studies in the esoteric and physical sciences, mathematics, comparative religion, art history, and symbolism reflect a deep curiosity about the nature of reality. With a foundation in architectural and color design, she explores the energetic principles behind form and perception.

Having lived in Egypt for 15 years and traveled extensively worldwide, Patricia continues to research ancient symbolism and the legacy of an advanced, spiritually evolved civilization that once connected humanity.

settings.title: How many megalithic temples are in Malta?
settings.text: Malta is home to seven megalithic temple sites, recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites. These include Ġgantija, Ħaġar Qim, Mnajdra, Tarxien, Ta' Ħaġrat, Skorba, and Borg in-Nadur.

settings.title: What is the history behind the megalithic temples of Malta?
settings.text: Dating back to 3600–2500 BCE, Malta’s megalithic temples are among the oldest free-standing structures, predating the pyramids and Stonehenge. Built by a prehistoric civilization, they were used for religious and astronomical rituals. Their advanced architecture, including corbelled walls, altars, and carvings, showcases the engineering skills of Malta’s early builders.
